No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** The fix remains useful: current main still learns installation status only after setup. The previously reported shipped-app compatibility regression remains unfixed on the unchanged head. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `ec6ef00c91fcef970d5d7962d995fa9f2bf24784` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Useful implementation and clear visual evidence are held back by the unresolved shipped-bridge regression. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Not applicable: The ordinary external-contributor gate does not apply to this member-authored PR. Inspected screenshots show the intended settings presentation through a synthetic bridge; the separate CLI observation does not demonstrate native bridge execution or shipped-app upgrade compatibility. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The ordinary external-contributor gate does not apply to this member-authored PR. Inspected screenshots show the intended settings presentation through a synthetic bridge; the separate CLI observation does not demonstrate native bridge execution or shipped-app upgrade compatibility. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Introduced setup gate: The introduced needsSetup condition requires a successful status result. A rejected status request leaves the result null and removes the installation button. The previous review examined the identical head; the finding remains applicable.
Released native request contract: The v2026.9.5 request decoder accepts install-chrome-extension but rejects chrome-extension-status. The released message handler replies with Invalid device settings request when decoding fails.
Released reply and upgrade contract: The released installation reply contains nativeHostRegistered, installRequested, and discoveredProfiles, without installedProfiles. Its stable Gateway compatibility rule accepts newer versions within the same major, so updating the Gateway can deliver this dashboard to an older Mac bridge. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Preserve Chrome setup for shipped Mac app versions | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Gateway serves the settings dashboard inside the Mac app, whose native bridge runs the local Chrome extension CLI. Discovery results determine the installation status and available setup actions. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Gateway settings dashboard] --> B[Mac device bridge] B --> C[Local extension CLI] C --> D[Chrome profiles and helper registration] D --> E[Installation status] E --> F[Installed or enablement guidance] E --> G[Setup or repair action] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve Chrome setup for shipped Mac app versions (P1)** - When the v2026.9.5 Mac app loads this dashboard from an updated Gateway, its native bridge rejects `chrome-extension-status`. The result stays null, so this condition removes the previously working setup button permanently. The shipped app accepts newer stable Gateways. Preserve setup when status is unsupported and accept the existing installation reply, which lacks the newly required `installedProfiles` field. Cover this released-app/new-dashboard combination. This prior finding remains unfixed on the same head. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - A Gateway upgrade can remove working in-app Chrome setup for v2026.9.5 Mac users; the submitted validation does not cover that mixed-version combination. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Restore setup for Mac bridges without status support, accept their existing installation replies, and validate released-app and updated-app behavior. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ## Findings - [P1] Preserve Chrome setup for shipped Mac app versions — `ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts:199-201`

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Native wire contract** | 1 new request; 1 newly required reply field | The independently installed Mac app can lag the Gateway-served dashboard. | | **Production versus test growth** | Production +125 net lines; tests +198 net lines | Production growth supports discovery and request lifecycle handling; coverage exercises status states but omits the released bridge. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `migration/backfill/repair: ui/src/i18n/locales/en-settings.ts`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Preserve shipped bridge compatibility (recommended)** Keep setup available without status support, accept the released installation reply, and verify both released and updated Mac bridges.
Copy recommended automerge instruction ```text @clawsweeper automerge Special instructions: Preserve Chrome setup with the v2026.9.5 Mac bridge when chrome-extension-status is unsupported, accept its installation reply without installedProfiles, and add focused mixed-version regression coverage while retaining updated-bridge discovery and stale-response protection. ```
### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep automatic discovery on capable Mac bridges while preserving the shipped installation action and reply contract on older apps. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: load the new dashboard with the v2026.9.5 native bridge, whose status rejection leaves setup hidden. This read-only review did not execute the application. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The existing CLI discovery owner is the right solution, but the dashboard must retain compatibility with the shipped native installation contract. Full review comments: - [P1] Preserve Chrome setup for shipped Mac app versions — `ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts:199-201` When the v2026.9.5 Mac app loads this dashboard from an updated Gateway, its native bridge rejects `chrome-extension-status`. The result stays null, so this condition removes the previously working setup button permanently. The shipped app accepts newer stable Gateways. Preserve setup when status is unsupported and accept the existing installation reply, which lacks the newly required `installedProfiles` field. Cover this released-app/new-dashboard combination. This prior finding remains unfixed on the same head. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.98 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. ([`ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts:201`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec6ef00c91fcef970d5d7962d995fa9f2bf24784/ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts#L201), [ec6ef00c91fc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec6ef00c91fcef970d5d7962d995fa9f2bf24784)) - **Released native request contract:** The v2026.9.5 request decoder accepts install-chrome-extension but rejects chrome-extension-status. The released message handler replies with Invalid device settings request when decoding fails. ([`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceSettingsContract.swift:160`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceSettingsContract.swift#L160), [ec9c1a13db89](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9)) - **Released reply and upgrade contract:** The released installation reply contains nativeHostRegistered, installRequested, and discoveredProfiles, without installedProfiles. Its stable Gateway compatibility rule accepts newer versions within the same major, so updating the Gateway can deliver this dashboard to an older Mac bridge. ([`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ChromeExtensionSetup.swift:4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ChromeExtensionSetup.swift#L4), [ec9c1a13db89](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9)) - **Mandatory new reply field survives merge:** The new shared result schema requires installedProfiles for installation replies as well as status replies. Inspection of the verified test merge against its recorded main parent confirms this change survives the merge. ([`ui/src/app/native-device-settings.ts:196`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/440fd5538a5d19cd6950ef86d22570a004889218/ui/src/app/native-device-settings.ts#L196), [440fd5538a5d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/440fd5538a5d19cd6950ef86d22570a004889218)) - **Current-main necessity:** At the fetched main revision, the settings card still renders the setup button unconditionally and obtains extension information only through installation. The relevant production files match the PR merge-base versions; the central improvement is not already implemented there. ([`ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts:187`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/572ef2ce9b3fb97ebd7f832921aa986d5ec7e4b6/ui/src/pages/device/device-page.ts#L187), [572ef2ce9b3f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/572ef2ce9b3fb97ebd7f832921aa986d5ec7e4b6)) - **Existing discovery owner and security boundary:** The new native action invokes the existing read-only browser extension status command. Browser-plugin discovery already separates Store installation from enablement. Native requests retain main-frame, trusted-document, current-session, and cancellation checks; no Codex dependency contract is involved. ([`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ChromeExtensionSetup.swift:60`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec6ef00c91fcef970d5d7962d995fa9f2bf24784/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ChromeExtensionSetup.swift#L60), [ec6ef00c91fc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec6ef00c91fcef970d5d7962d995fa9f2bf24784)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 8964a4d8dc2f24979c773fbf96bc4a3ca79ed5f2 adds apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ChromeExtensionSetup.swift:43 relative to its recorded parents.
